hard_gates.gate: G2 catches faults planted in p06's surface
hard_gates.evidence: Two permission faults in this piece's own export and print code passed every gate test. P6 makes CSV and XLSX exports ignore the caller's withheld columns (plants/plant-P6-exports-ignore-withheld-columns.patch): in run A all G2 tests passed, and only L4's G1 tests failed. P8 makes list printing name another area's records without checking that the caller may read that list (plants/plant-P8-list-print-names-without-permission.patch): in run B all G2 tests passed, and only L5's G1 tests failed. Both are real on a planted live stack (plants/plant-P6-P8-live-demo.txt). A user holding only identity.users.read plus reports.catalog.read received the 'Role' and 'Only in company' columns in the usersByRole CSV (the JSON for the same request withholds them). In the printed users list, the Roles column showed 'Administrator' instead of a count. /api/identity/roles answers that user 403. The cause: G2ReportData judges reports only at format=json, and no gate judges what list prints contain. W3 (textarea ignores readOnly) is not counted: a disabled fieldset disables it anyway.

biggest_gap.title: The permission gate never reads exports or list printouts: role data withheld from a user still goes out in their CSV and printed lists, and every gate passes
biggest_gap.detail: For a UAE trading company, exports and printouts are how data leaves the system: Excel to the accountant, PDFs to auditors. This piece owns that surface. The gate passes any export or printout that contains columns or record names the caller's roles do not grant. G2ReportData judges reports only as format=json, so a CSV/XLSX export that ignores the withheld columns (P6) passes. No gate judges what /api/reports/lists/<key> prints, so a list print that names another area's records without checking the caller may read them (P8) passes. Round 2 fixed the server plants of rounds 1 and 2, but only for JSON and report runs. The gate should run every report and every printable list in every format (json, pdf after text extraction, csv, xlsx) and both languages, as users holding exactly the report's or list's permission (and each extra read permission). Every value printed, record names in ValuesFrom columns included, must also be shown by an endpoint those permissions open. The gate should be plant-tested with P6 and P8.
biggest_gap.evidence: plants/plant-P6-exports-ignore-withheld-columns.patch (ReportEndpoints.RunAsync: Withheld = empty for csv/xlsx) and plants/plant-P8-list-print-names-without-permission.patch (ReportEndpoints.NamesAsync: the caller.Has(source.List.Permission) check removed), applied to cb26098. other_findings: The 'Roles and access' report (identity.roleSummary, p06's totals report) gives wrong user counts and totals. It counts only workspace-wide role assignments (RoleSummaryReport.cs:44, db.UserRoles) and ignores per-company roles (identity.user_company_roles). On screen and in PDF: Company manager 0 users, Read-only 1, grand total 4. The roles list and the database say Company manager 1, Read-only 2, total 6, and the Users by role report shows Hessa Al Suwaidi holding Company manager in ALN-DXB (07-report-role-summary-en.jpg vs 06-report-users-by-role-en.jpg and 11-pdf-roles-list-ar.jpg). It is the same class as p03's flaw: per-company roles are ignored. [route: p03-users-roles] for the counting rule.

The OpenAPI document gives report and list-print endpoints no media types or schema for 200 (no application/json ReportDocument, application/pdf, text/csv or xlsx). A client cannot learn the JSON document's shape from the documented API.

Users list and report exports print the Status column as 'Yes'/'No' (Arabic 'نعم'/'لا') under the header 'Status'. They should say Active/Inactive.
